question.worked_solution:
Since we have an overall common factor of $2$, we start by dividing our equation through by $2.$ This gives 

$$
4{u}^{3}-3{u}^{2}-36u+27=0.
$$

Next, we factor by grouping. Notice that when grouping the smaller terms, we factor out the negative sign.

$$
\begin{aligned}4{u}^{3}-3{u}^{2}-36u+27 & = \\ (4{u}^{3}-3{u}^{2})-(36u-27) & = \\ {u}^{2}(4u-3)-9(4u-3) & = \\ (4u-3)\cdot {u}^{2}-(4u-3)\cdot 9 & = \\ (4u-3)({u}^{2}-9) & .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we set each factor equal to $0$ and solve:

- Setting the factor $(4u-3)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4u-3 & =0 \\ 4u & =3 \\ u & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Setting the factor $({u}^{2}-9)$ equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}-9 & =0 \\ {u}^{2} & =9 \\ u & =\pm 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  the solutions to the given equation are $\frac{3}{4}$ and $\pm 3.$
